findings.reason: `sprint_liveness._recorded_states` (reckon/sprint_liveness.py:66) and `mcp_views._recorded_live_run_classifications` (reckon/mcp_views.py:1813) both open `runs.watch_stream_path(project)`, one `*.events` file per project (reckon/crew/run_paths.py:31-33), and `parse_stream_line` is called nowhere else on the roadmap path, so the profile's own arithmetic (194,212 from `_recorded_states` = 2 × 97,106 from `_recorded_live_run_classifications`) describes one watch stream read three times per process, not ten per-run streams; with no watch stream in the fixture both readers return `{}`, the count passes at head and at base alike, and this is the same fail-open shape the previous review found in §28's first count.
findings.text: §30's done-when fixtures per-run streams and bounds parses by "the total line count" of those ten streams, while the two readers it names open one project-level watch stream, so a test built as written counts zero parses and its negative control cannot fail

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §30's done-when builds "ten live pointers whose streams hold at least 1,000 lines each", but the two readers it names open one project-level watch stream, so the count and its control measure an object the readers never open.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both nodes name durable write paths (`reckon/ledger.py`, `reckon/mcp_views.py`, `reckon/sprint_liveness.py`, `reckon/crew/runs.py` and their test files) and log their controls under the run directory; no session-scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §28 and §30 carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into a symbol, file or comment, and state the mechanism rather than a tracker entry.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §28's root cause holds against its cited evidence (the live node has no last-good index, so `load` falls past reckon/ledger.py:1392-1401 into the per-file scan at 1411), and §30's mechanism runs on the real path with its caller named (`mcp._roadmap` reaches `sprint_liveness._recorded_states` and, through `mcp_views.partition_live_runs`, `_recorded_live_run_classifications`). The one reasoning consequence that does not hold — the mechanism's scoping against its own fixture — is carried below under done_when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §28 carries one measure (run files read, and `ledger.load` calls, against the index) and §30 one measure (stream parses per read); §28's exception capture is a prerequisite of that measure, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §28 states "Build it after §22" and §30 "Build it after §29", and both named sections exist and write the module each depends on (`reckon/ledger.py`, `reckon/sprint_liveness.py`).
